content: 1. Famotidine, calcium carbonate, and magnesium hydroxide should be chewed completely before swallowing. Do not exceed 2 tablets within a 24-hour period. 2. Intravenous ceftriaxone should not be used with any calcium-containing solutions (e.g., Ringer or Hartmann solutions) due to the risk of potentially fatal particulate precipitation in the lungs and kidneys. Separate administration by at least 48 hours. 3. Calcium carbonate decreases the level or effect of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations when antacids or buffered medications are coadministered. 4. Famotidine decreases the level or effect of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Substantially reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir are expected if H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs) are coadministered. For treatment-naïve patients, atazanavir should be taken simultaneously with the H2RA or at least 10 hours afterward. Dosage adjustments are recommended for treatment-experienced patients. 5. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the level or effect of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, resulting in decreased absorption. Studies in monkeys showed significantly decreased plasma levels when coadministered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 6. Calcium carbonate decreases the level or effect of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
